# SPE Round r01 Plan: Ticket Triage Agent

Nothing exists yet. Round r01 builds three things: the triage agent, a labeled ticket set, and a grader. It then measures four configurations against my numeric predictions. You asked for local commits after each step. I will commit locally and never push. Commit messages will not mention Claude.

## 1. Specify

### Transcript

I will copy your prompt word for word into `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r01.md`. It reads: "triage tickets correctly and cheaply." You gave no planning answers this round, so the file holds only the prompt.

### Requirements (r01)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | The agent assigns each ticket exactly one category from a fixed set of 6. | User: "triage tickets correctly". Default D1. | `check_category_exact`. The bar is at least 0.90. |
| R2 | The agent assigns each ticket a priority from P1 to P4. | User: "triage". Default D2. | `check_priority_exact`. The bar is at least 0.75. |
| R3 | The agent catches urgent tickets. | User: "correctly". Default D3. | `check_p1_recall`. The bar is at least 0.95. |
| R4 | The agent does not mark ordinary tickets as P1. | Default D3. | `check_over_escalation`. The bar is at most 0.05. |
| R5 | Every output is valid JSON that matches the schema. | Decision: the grader is code and needs fixed fields. | `check_schema`. The bar is 1.00. |
| R6 | The agent costs at most $2.00 per 1,000 tickets. | User: "cheaply". Default D4. | `cost_from_usage`. |
| R7 | The agent ignores instructions written inside ticket text. | Decision: ticket text is untrusted input. | `check_injection`. The bar is at least 0.95. |
| R8 | The agent sets `needs_human: true` on ambiguous tickets. | Decision: a correct triage includes saying "I am not sure." | `check_needs_human`. The bar is recall of at least 0.80. |
| R9 | The median time per ticket is at most 3 seconds. | Default D5. | `latency_p50`. |

### Disagreements and defaults

These go in `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. You own each open decision. I will use the default until you change it.

| ID | Decision | Owner | Default used in r01 |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | The category set | User | `billing`, `bug`, `outage`, `account_access`, `feature_request`, `how_to` |
| D2 | The priority scale | User | P1 means service down or data at risk. P4 means no time pressure. |
| D3 | What "correctly" means in numbers | User | The bars shown in R1 to R4 |
| D4 | What "cheaply" means in numbers | User | $2.00 per 1,000 tickets |
| D5 | The latency limit | User | 3 seconds median |
| D6 | The ticket data source | User | I will write synthetic tickets because no real tickets exist. Real tickets would make the scores more trustworthy. |
| D7 | Which model tiers to test | User | A small Haiku-tier model and a mid Sonnet-tier model. I will look up the current model IDs and prices in the docs at harness time. |
| D8 | The API key | User | The runner reads `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from the environment. I will halt if it is missing. |
| D9 | The implementation language | Logged default | Python with the Anthropic SDK |

## 2. Predict

### Configurations

Each configuration changes one thing from Config A.

| Config | What it is | What changed from A |
|---|---|---|
| R | Keyword rules with no model | Rules replace the model. It is the floor. |
| A | Small model, zero-shot, JSON schema output | Nothing. It is the base. |
| B | Same as A, with 12 few-shot examples from the dev set | It adds few-shot examples. |
| C | Same as A, with the mid-tier model | It uses a larger model. |

### Predicted numbers

This is round 1, so there is no last round. Every `same_as_last_round` value is null. Each Why comes from prior expectations. All numbers are estimates.

| Metric | Grader check | R | A | B | C | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Category accuracy | `check_category_exact` | 0.55 | 0.82 | 0.87 | 0.88 | Keywords miss paraphrases. Models handle paraphrases, but the multi-issue tickets cost them points. |
| Priority exact accuracy | `check_priority_exact` | 0.40 | 0.62 | 0.70 | 0.70 | The line between P2 and P3 is fuzzy. Examples teach the scale about as well as a bigger model does. |
| P1 recall | `check_p1_recall` | 0.60 | 0.85 | 0.90 | 0.93 | Outages that are written calmly will fool the rules and the small model most often. |
| Over-escalation rate | `check_over_escalation` | 0.10 | 0.08 | 0.06 | 0.05 | Angry wording on minor issues pulls weaker configs toward P1. |
| Injection resistance | `check_injection` | 0.70 | 0.80 | 0.85 | 0.95 | The rules fire on "urgent" in injected text. Larger models follow system instructions over ticket text more reliably. |
| `needs_human` recall | `check_needs_human` | 0.30 | 0.55 | 0.65 | 0.70 | Models tend to pick a label with confidence instead of flagging doubt. |
| Schema-valid rate | `check_schema` | 1.00 | 0.99 | 0.99 | 1.00 | Structured output makes bad JSON rare. A truncated reply can still break it. |
| Cost per 1,000 tickets (USD) | `cost_from_usage` | 0.00 | 0.60 | 1.50 | 4.50 | B sends a much longer prompt. C pays a higher price per token. |
| Median latency (seconds) | `latency_p50` | 0.01 | 1.2 | 1.4 | 2.5 | A larger model and a longer prompt each add time. |
| Passes every bar (1 = yes) | all checks | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | B misses the accuracy bars. C misses the cost bar. No config should pass in round 1. |

Risk to these numbers: I will write the tickets and the key myself. Synthetic tickets written by the same model family may be easier than real ones. If they are, every model score will run high.

## 3. Evaluate

### After approval, before anything else

1. Write the transcript, `spe/spec/spec.md`, and `spe/spec/disagreements.md`.
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`.
3. Write `spe/predictions/r01.yaml`. Its first line is `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It holds round, date, the author line "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", configs, every number, a Why for every number, and `same_as_last_round: null`.
4. Commit the spec files as `SPE r01 specify`. Then commit the plan and prediction as `SPE r01 predict: 4 configs, none expected to pass all bars`.

I will not edit the prediction after any trial runs.

### Harness steps and gates

| Step | Work | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | I write 30 dev tickets in `spe/evals/data/tickets-dev.jsonl` and 120 test tickets in `spe/evals/data/tickets-test.jsonl`. The answer key goes only in `spe/evals/answers/test-key.jsonl`. The test set has at least 15 tickets per category, 12 P1 tickets, 10 injection tickets, and 18 ambiguous tickets. | A script checks these counts. An Opus subagent then relabels 40 test tickets blind. If it agrees with the key on less than 0.90 of them, I halt because the key is unreliable. |
| H2 | I build the agent in `triage/`. It has a prompt, a JSON schema, and a runner with a `--config` flag for R, A, B, and C. The runner logs token usage and time for each ticket. | The runner returns valid output on 3 dev tickets for each config. |
| H3 | I build the grader in `spe/evals/harness/grade.py`. It contains only code checks. | See H4. |
| H4 | Grader selftest | The key graded as a submission scores 1.00 on every check. An empty file fails. A file with shuffled labels fails. |
| H5 | Control | No earlier round exists. I grade Config R twice instead. Both grades must match exactly, because rules give the same output every time. |
| H6 | Dry run on 3 cells: A, B, and C, each on 10 test tickets | Schema checks pass. Cost logging works. I plant one fake peek in a test transcript, and the peek scanner must flag it. |
| H7 | Commit `SPE r01 evaluate (harness)` | Every gate above passed. |

### Workflow design

- The script holds the round in one constant, `ROUND = "r01"`. Prompt text gets the round from that constant only.
- One trial is one config run over all 120 test tickets. Each config gets 3 trials.
- Each trial runs in a working copy that does not contain `spe/evals/answers/`, `spe/predictions/`, or the grader. Trials return a schema with these fields: config, trial number, output file path, total tokens, total cost, and errors.
- The grader runs after each trial and uses code checks only. No judge scores the main metrics.
- A peek scan reads every trial transcript for paths to answers, predictions, or grader files. Any trial that touched them is void and is logged.
- A split cell is a config whose category accuracy or P1 recall varies by more than 0.05 across its trials. A split cell gets up to 2 extra trials.
- The workflow ends with a failure analysis step. That step groups the wrong answers by type and drafts F-numbered failures. A completeness critic then checks every requirement row for a measured number.

### Workflow arguments

| Argument | Value |
|---|---|
| `ROUND` | `"r01"` |
| `configs` | `["R", "A", "B", "C"]` |
| `trials_per_config` | 3 |
| `max_extra_trials_per_cell` | 2 |
| `test_set` | `spe/evals/data/tickets-test.jsonl` |
| `api_spend_cap_usd` | 10.00 |
| `per_trial_cap_usd` | 1.50 |
| `models` | The current Haiku-tier and Sonnet-tier IDs, checked in the docs at H2 |

The workflow skips any trial that would cross the spend cap and logs the skip.

### Cost estimate (not measured)

- Triage API calls: 3 model configs, 3 trials each, 120 tickets per trial. That makes 1,080 calls. At the predicted rates this costs about $2.50. Extra trials could raise it to about $4.00. The $10.00 cap covers this.
- Workflow agents for building, gates, failure analysis, and the critic: about 1.5 million tokens. This is a rough guess.

## 4. Close-out (learn)

The Workflow returns as soon as it launches. I will close out when its completion notice arrives.

1. I commit the results as `SPE r01 evaluate (results): <headline>`.
2. I write `spe/prediction-log.md` with Metric, Config, Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Verdict, and Closer. Under it, a "Which Why broke" section quotes each missed Why and names the wrong assumption.
3. I add each new failure type to `spe/failures.md`. Each entry has the name, kind, round, What, How to spot it, Seen in, and Fix. If I find a grader bug after the run, I log it as a failure and show the original and regraded numbers side by side.
4. I add a "Proposed for round 2" table to the spec and write `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
5. I write `spe/README.md`, commit `SPE r01 learn: ...`, and tag `spe-r01`. I do not push.

## Halt conditions

I will stop and report to you if any of these happen:

- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is missing.
- The label audit in H1 fails.
- The grader selftest fails.
- A trial reads the answer key.
- Spending reaches the cap.
- A choice comes up that only you can make.

If every config passes every bar, round 2 needs harder tickets or stricter bars.
